# Eidos Works

Eidos Works designs digital experiences and operational tools for organizations with complicated real-world workflows. Brent Parent is the founder, designer, developer, and operator behind the work.

## Primary topics
- Digital experience design and frontend development
- Hosted storefront and employee access systems
- Operational dashboards and workflow automation
- Structured content and search-readiness
- Proof-stage Eidos Brain research with human review

## Insights
- [The Storefront Proof Loop Connects UX, Assets, and Operations](https://eidos-works.com/insights/storefront-proof-loop-ux-assets-operations): A strategic framework for connecting storefront UX, Cloudinary-ready assets, production workflow reality, and post-launch content into one stronger commerce system.
- [A Practical Source Map for AI-Ready Service Pages](https://eidos-works.com/insights/practical-source-map-ai-ready-service-pages): How to structure service pages so customers, search engines, and AI-assisted discovery systems can understand the offer.
- [What Agentic SEO Means for Small Business Websites](https://eidos-works.com/insights/agentic-seo-small-business-websites): A plain-language guide to making a small-business website easier for customers, search engines, and AI assistants to understand.
- [How to Structure a Website So People and AI Assistants Understand It](https://eidos-works.com/insights/structure-website-people-ai-assistants-understand): A practical framework for turning a collection of pages into a clear path for visitors, search systems, and AI-assisted discovery.
- [Storefront UX: Helping Customers Find the Right Product Faster](https://eidos-works.com/insights/storefront-ux-find-right-product-faster): How stronger categories, product context, ordering guidance, and mobile paths can make a hosted or custom storefront easier to shop.
- [From Spreadsheet Chaos to Operational Dashboards](https://eidos-works.com/insights/spreadsheet-chaos-operational-dashboards): A grounded way to decide when a spreadsheet needs a clearer operational view—and what a useful dashboard should show first.
- [What a Website Snapshot Can Tell You Before a Redesign](https://eidos-works.com/insights/website-snapshot-before-redesign): What an early website concept and focused recommendation report can clarify—and what still requires a full audit, design process, and build.
- [Why Mobile Hierarchy Matters More Than Desktop Polish](https://eidos-works.com/insights/mobile-hierarchy-over-desktop-polish): Why the order, spacing, and priority of information on a small screen often matter more than the most polished desktop presentation.
- [Baseline 2026 Turns Browser Support Into a Design-System Decision](https://eidos-works.com/insights/baseline-2026-browser-support-design-system-decision): How Eidos Works uses Baseline, MDN compatibility signals, and progressive enhancement to decide which modern interface features are ready for production sites.
- [Eidos Brain and Sentinel: A Small-Business Intelligence Model](https://eidos-works.com/insights/eidos-brain-sentinel-small-business-intelligence): A grounded case note on using signals, exceptions, readable briefs, and human review to make small-business intelligence useful.
